question: In which year did Raja Ram Mohan Roy found the Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1815.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy launched the Atmiya Sabha in 1815 as a forum for discussing monotheism and attacking idol worship, caste rigidity and social evils (आत्मीय सभा की स्थापना, 1815)

 

• The Sabha held debates on Upanishadic philosophy and the irrationality of ritualism, drawing educated Bengalis around Roy.

 

• It was the first of his organisational efforts and prepared the ground for the Brahmo Sabha of August 1828.

 

• Roy's later bodies therefore trace back to this 1815 society, which makes it the starting point of his institutional reform work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmo Sabha of 20 August 1828 later became the Brahmo Samaj, with Debendranath Tagore reviving it after 1843.

 

• Roy also edited Samvad Kaumudi (Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Persian), the two journals carrying his campaigns.

 

• He is called the Father of the Indian Renaissance and the Father of Modern India.

 

• Roy's Vedanta Society (1816) is sometimes counted among his early efforts, though its date is less certain than the Atmiya Sabha's. Debendranath Tagore's Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) later carried the Brahmo mission forward in Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• 1828 (Option 1): 1828 is the year the Brahmo Sabha, the later Brahmo Samaj, was started by Roy; the Atmiya Sabha was an earlier society that preceded it by about thirteen years.

 

• 1816 (Option 3): 1816 does not mark the Atmiya Sabha, though it is the year commonly given for Roy's Vedanta Society; the question concerns the earlier discussion circle begun in 1815.

 

• 1875 (Option 4): 1875 belongs to the Arya Samaj of Dayanand Saraswati and the Theosophical Society; Roy had died in 1833, so he could not have founded anything then.

question: The first Bengali weekly newspaper Samvad Kaumudi was started by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy started the Bengali weekly Samvad Kaumudi and also edited the Persian weekly Mirat-ul-Akhbar (संवाद कौमुदी — राजा राममोहन राय का बंगाली साप्ताहिक)

 

• Through Samvad Kaumudi he conducted his campaign against the practice of Sati, reasoning from scripture that widow burning had no sanction.

 

• His journalism made him a pioneer of the Indian press as an instrument of social reform and public opinion.

 

• Roy's writing in both Bengali and Persian reached the zamindari, scholarly and official classes of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roy's Mirat-ul-Akhbar was among the earliest Persian periodicals of India and he protested against press restrictions of 1823.

 

• Derozio edited the East Indian and Hesperus, journals of his own Young Bengal circle.

 

• Vidyasagar edited the Somprakash in later decades and helped manage Tattvabodhini Patrika affairs.

 

• Roy opposed the Press Regulation of 1823 that required licences for newspapers, and his protest is seen as a landmark in the early struggle for freedom of the press in India. Mirat-ul-Akhbar appeared in 1822.

 

NOTE

 

• Henry Vivian Derozio (Option 1): Henry Vivian Derozio led the Young Bengal circle and wrote poetry and edited the East Indian; Samvad Kaumudi, however, was launched in 1821 when Derozio was still a boy, so he cannot be its founder.

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 2): Debendranath Tagore ran the Tattvabodhini Sabha and its Patrika from 1839 and reorganised the Brahmo Samaj, but Samvad Kaumudi was a creation of his predecessor Roy.

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 4): Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a Sanskrit scholar and educator campaigning for widow remarriage; his writing appeared in other periodicals and not in the early Bengali weekly Samvad Kaumudi.

question: Who bestowed the title of 'Raja' on Ram Mohan Roy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mughal emperor Akbar II conferred the title Raja on Ram Mohan Roy and sent him to England as his envoy to plead the case for an increase in the emperor's allowance (अकबर द्वितीय ने रॉय को 'राजा' की उपाधि दी)

 

• The Mughal ruler was then only a titular king under the Company's protection, so the title was honorary and symbolic.

 

• Roy accepted the mission and, as the emperor's representative, went to England where he later died at Bristol in 1833.

 

• The episode shows his standing among the Mughal court as well as among reform circles in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roy appeared before the Select Committee of the British Parliament and gave evidence on Indian conditions during the 1833 Charter Act debate.

 

• He opposed the Press Regulation of 1823 and defended Indian rights to higher English education.

 

• Roy assisted David Hare in the foundation of Hindu College, Calcutta (1817).

 

• Roy sailed for England in 1830 as the envoy of the Mughal emperor, and the visit also let him witness the debates on the renewal of the Company's Charter. He is buried at Arnos Vale in Bristol.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 1): Lord William Bentinck, Governor-General (1828-35), banned Sati in 1829 largely under Roy's influence, but he had no authority to confer a title on behalf of the Mughal court.

 

• Bahadur Shah II (Option 2): Bahadur Shah II was the last Mughal emperor (1837-57) and succeeded Akbar II after Roy's death in 1833, so he could not have granted Roy any title in the 1820s.

 

• William IV (Option 3): William IV was the British monarch (1830-37) whom Roy was asked to meet on behalf of Akbar II; he was the recipient of the petition, not the one who awarded the title.

question:
Consider the following statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy:

1. He opposed the supremacy of Brahmin priests and favoured inter-caste marriages.

2. He founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875.

3. He assisted David Hare in founding Hindu College, Calcutta.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Roy rejected priestly dominance, supported inter-caste marriage and adopted a Muslim boy himself, showing his rejection of caste barriers (केवल कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं)

 

• Statement 2 is wrong: the Arya Samaj was set up by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, long after Roy's death in 1833.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Roy helped David Hare establish Hindu College in Calcutta (1817), for imparting Western education.

 

• Roy's own organisations were Atmiya Sabha (1815) and Brahmo Sabha (1828).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindu College later became Presidency College, Calcutta, a leading centre of English education.

 

• Roy believed in monotheism and drew on Upanishadic ideas, Christian ethics and Islamic unitarian thought.

 

• Dayanand's Arya Samaj later shifted its main centre to Lahore.

 

• Roy's belief in one formless God drew on the Upanishads, the Quran-based unitarianism he studied in Persian and Arabic, and Christian ethics, and he published 'The Precepts of Jesus' in 1820.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 2): The combination of 1 and 2 wrongly credits Roy with the Arya Samaj, which Dayanand Saraswati founded in 1875, while omitting his true role in Hindu College's foundation.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): The combination of 2 and 3 repeats the error about the Arya Samaj and drops statement 1, although Roy did oppose Brahmin priestly supremacy and favoured intercaste marriage.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Including all three statements is wrong because statement 2 cannot hold: Roy died in 1833, forty-two years before the Arya Samaj appeared in 1875 under Dayanand.

question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy launched a campaign against Sati after his sister-in-law immolated herself on his brother's death. Which method did he mainly use?
option_4: Petitions to the Mughal court only
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newspapers and public debates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roy campaigned mainly through newspapers, writings and public debates, notably his journal Samvad Kaumudi, showing from scriptures that Sati had no real sanction (अख़बारों और बहस के माध्यम से सती-विरोधी अभियान)

 

• The incident of 1818, when his Bhabhi was burnt on his brother's pyre, turned his concern into a public movement.

 

• His agitation helped persuade Governor-General Lord William Bentinck to pass Regulation XVII in 1829, declaring Sati illegal and punishable.

 

• The method was constitutional and persuasive rather than violent, typical of early nineteenth-century reformers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1829 regulation applied first to Bengal Presidency and was extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830.

 

• Orthodox Hindus led by Radhakanta Deb formed the Dharma Sabha to oppose the law and petitioned the Privy Council.

 

• The Privy Council rejected the appeal in 1832.

 

• The Sati regulation of 1829 was extended to the Bombay and Madras presidencies in 1830. Orthodox Hindus, led by Radhakanta Deb, organised the Dharma Sabha in Calcutta to protest, but the Privy Council rejected their appeal in 1832.

 

NOTE

 

• Armed protests against zamindars (Option 1): Armed protests were not part of Roy's technique; he used rational argument and publicity, and the campaign relied on influencing the government rather than on force.

 

• Alliances with Christian missionaries (Option 3): Roy did cooperate with some Unitarian Christians in Calcutta on other matters, but the Sati campaign was fought through his own journals and debates, not through any alliance with missionaries.

 

• Petitions to the Mughal court only (Option 4): The petitions were not directed to a Mughal court that had no real legal power by the 1820s; the authority to ban Sati lay with the British Governor-General.

question: Who founded the Young Bengal Movement and taught at Hindu College, Calcutta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Vivian Derozio.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Vivian Derozio (born in Calcutta, 1809), a teacher at Hindu College, inspired the radical Young Bengal group of students (हेनरी विवियन डेरोज़ियो — यंग बंगाल आंदोलन के प्रणेता)

 

• His followers attacked old traditions and decadent customs, questioned religion through free reasoning and debated freely on issues like liberty and equality.

 

• They also advocated women's rights and education, making the movement more radical than Roy's moderate reformism.

 

• Derozio's dismissal from the college in 1831 under orthodox pressure and his early death the same year did not end the circle's influence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Young Bengal members were also called Derozians and founded the Academic Association for discussion.

 

• Derozio's ideas drew on the French Revolution and the Enlightenment.

 

• The movement lacked a lasting organisation and mass support, so its impact stayed limited to a small educated group.

 

• Derozio's Academic Association met regularly at his home to debate on God, free will and patriotism. He also wrote poetry, including 'The Fakeer of Jungheera', and is regarded as India's first modern national poet in English.

 

NOTE

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 1): Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a Sanskrit College principal and champion of widow remarriage and girls' education; he came to prominence after Derozio's death and was not part of the Young Bengal circle.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 2): Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj of India after the 1866 split and was born in 1838, so he was far too young to have founded Young Bengal in the 1820s.

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 4): Debendranath Tagore revived the Brahmo Sabha and led the Adi Brahmo Samaj, a religious reform body that stood for Upanishadic theism rather than the rationalist radicalism of Derozio's students.

question: What was the childhood name of Swami Dayanand Saraswati, who was born in Kathiawar, Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mool Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (1824-1883), born in Kathiawar (Gujarat), was originally called Mool Shankar (दयानंद सरस्वती का बचपन का नाम मूलशंकर)

 

• He became a sannyasi and a student of Swami Virajananda of Mathura, who directed him to revive pure Vedic religion.

 

• His motto 'Back to the Vedas' regarded the Vedas as the source of all true knowledge.

 

• He founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 at Bombay and wrote the Satyarth Prakash.

 

• Dayanand's identity as a sannyasi came after he left home at about twenty-one to avoid marriage, and he spent years wandering among yogis before meeting his teacher at Mathura.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Satyarth Prakash (1875) is often called the Bible of the Arya Samaj; he also wrote a commentary on the Rigveda (Rigveda Bhasya).

 

• Narendra Nath Dutt was the original name of Vivekananda and Gadadhar Chattopadhyay of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.

 

• Dayanand died in 1883 at Ajmer.

 

• Dayanand's guru Swami Virajananda of Mathura taught him that the later Hindu texts had corrupted the Vedas. Dayanand died in 1883 at Ajmer, reportedly after being poisoned during a stay in the Jodhpur state.

 

NOTE

 

• Narendra Nath Dutt (Option 2): Narendra Nath Dutt was the name of Swami Vivekananda, born in Calcutta in 1863, who became the chief disciple of Ramakrishna; it has no connection with Dayanand of Kathiawar.

 

• Gadadhar Chattopadhyay (Option 3): Gadadhar Chattopadhyay was the early name of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, the priest of Dakshineswar, whose teachings inspired the Ramakrishna Mission; he was born in Bengal, not in Gujarat.

 

• Mohandas (Option 4): Mohandas is the first name of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, who was also born in Kathiawar region (Porbandar) but in 1869 and who was not a religious reformer founding any Samaj.

question: Dayanand Saraswati's ideas are contained in his book:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyarth Prakash.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satyarth Prakash (1875) sets out Dayanand's teachings, including attacks on idol worship, caste by birth and child marriage, and is often called the Bible of the Arya Samaj (सत्यार्थ प्रकाश — आर्य समाज का आधार ग्रंथ)

 

• Dayanand wrote it in Hindi so that ordinary people could read it, in contrast with Sanskrit-based scholarship.

 

• He also wrote the Rigveda Bhasya, a commentary on the Vedas, in support of his claim that the Vedas contain all knowledge.

 

• The book also criticised the beliefs of other religions, which made Arya Samaj controversial.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dayanand's slogans included 'Back to the Vedas' and 'India for Indians'.

 

• He launched the Suddhi (purification) movement for reconverting Hindus who had adopted other faiths.

 

• The first DAV school was started in Lahore in 1886 after his death.

 

• Satyarth Prakash was first written in Hindi in 1875 and revised in 1884. Dayanand also composed Rigveda Bhashya and Sanskar Vidhi, which lay down the Arya Samaj ceremonies in place of Brahmin ritual.

 

NOTE

 

• Gulamgiri (Option 1): Gulamgiri was written by Jyotiba Phule in 1873 to expose the oppression of lower castes by Brahmins; it is a work of social criticism, not Dayanand's doctrinal text.

 

• Samvad Kaumudi (Option 2): Samvad Kaumudi was the Bengali weekly newspaper edited by Raja Ram Mohan Roy; it was a journal, appeared decades earlier, and was not a book authored by Dayanand.

 

• Ananda Math (Option 3): Anandamath is a novel by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee (1882) that contains the song Vande Mataram; it deals with the Sannyasi rebellion theme, not with Arya Samaj doctrine.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Arya Samaj:

1. It was established at Bombay in 1875.

2. It supported widow remarriage and women's education.

3. It accepted idol worship as a path to salvation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 holds: Dayanand Saraswati established the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875 (आर्य समाज की स्थापना 1875, बंबई)

 

• Statement 2 holds: the Samaj stood for equal rights of men and women, women's education, widow remarriage and inter-caste marriage.

 

• Statement 3 fails: the movement strictly opposed idol worship, along with child marriage, untouchability and birth-based caste distinctions.

 

• So only the first two statements are valid.

 

• Arya Samaj also asked its members to give up Brahmin priests for ritual duties and substituted the Vedic fire ceremony (havan) for temple-based worship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj shifted its main base to Lahore in the Punjab, where it became very influential.

 

• Its educational wing built Dayanand Anglo-Vedic institutions; the first DAV school started at Lahore in 1886.

 

• The Samaj also ran gurukuls, such as the one at Kangri founded later by Swami Shraddhanand.

 

• After Dayanand's death the Samaj split into two camps: the 'college party' led by Lala Hansraj and Lajpat Rai and the 'Gurukul party' led by Swami Shraddhanand. Their dispute concerned English education against Vedic schooling.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Pairing statement 2 with statement 3 wrongly makes the Samaj tolerant of idol worship; the movement rejected image worship and believed in a formless God and Vedic ritual.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statement 1 with statement 3 correctly identifies the founding but accepts idol worship, which Dayanand fiercely opposed in his teaching.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three statements cannot be right because the third contradicts the central doctrine of the Arya Samaj, whose reformist message was built on the rejection of idols.

question: The Shuddhi (Suddhi) movement of the Arya Samaj aimed at:
option_2: Reconverting Hindus who had adopted other religions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reconverting Hindus who had adopted other religions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Suddhi movement, started by Dayanand and his followers, aimed at bringing back to Hinduism those who had converted to other religions (शुद्धि आंदोलन — पुनः हिंदू धर्म में वापसी)

 

• It was a response to proselytising activity by Christian missionaries and others.

 

• The movement made the Arya Samaj assertive and also created tensions with the Muslim and Christian communities in the Punjab and United Provinces.

 

• It was a religious activity of the Samaj, unrelated to economic boycott or Muslim education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Shraddhanand later became the best-known leader of Suddhi work in the 1920s.

 

• Shraddhanand also founded the Gurukul at Kangri.

 

• The Arya Samaj ran orphanages and famine relief besides its schools.

 

• Suddhi work later extended to Malkana Rajputs in the United Provinces in the 1920s, when communal tension rose. Swami Shraddhanand was assassinated in 1926 by a man angered by his conversion work.

 

NOTE

 

• Boycott of foreign goods (Option 1): Boycott of foreign goods was the economic programme of the Swadeshi Movement after the 1905 partition of Bengal, an unrelated nationalist campaign that came decades after Dayanand's death.

 

• Spreading English education among Muslims (Option 3): English education for Muslims was the mission of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's Aligarh Movement, which founded the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College in 1875; the Arya Samaj had a different purpose.

 

• Establishing temples for lower castes (Option 4): Temple entry for lower castes was a twentieth-century cause pursued by Gandhi and others such as Vaikom Satyagraha leaders; the Suddhi programme concerned reconversion, not temple access.

question: Where was the first Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) School founded in 1886?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lahore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first DAV School was opened in 1886 at Lahore, followed by the DAV College, with Lala Lajpat Rai and Lala Hansraj among its prominent organisers (लाहौर में पहला डी.ए.वी. स्कूल, 1886)

 

• The institutions sought to combine modern Western subjects with Vedic teachings after the death of Dayanand in 1883.

 

• Lahore became the stronghold of the Arya Samaj in the Punjab after its headquarters shifted there.

 

• The DAV network later spread across northern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lala Hansraj served as honorary principal of the DAV College, Lahore.

 

• The Samaj's gurukul wing later preferred traditional Vedic schooling, as at Haridwar.

 

• Dayanand himself had founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875.

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai, called Punjab Kesari, belonged to the Arya Samaj and later led the Congress extremists. He died in 1928 after being lathi-charged during the protest against the Simon Commission in Lahore.

 

NOTE

 

• Amritsar (Option 2): Amritsar saw the first Singh Sabha in 1873 and later the Khalsa College in 1892, both belonging to Sikh reform and not to the Arya Samaj's Anglo-Vedic school scheme.

 

• Bombay (Option 3): Bombay is where the Arya Samaj itself was founded in 1875 and where the Prarthana Samaj began in 1867, but the first DAV school was not set up there.

 

• Aligarh (Option 4): Aligarh is the seat of the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College begun by Sir Syed in 1875, which later became Aligarh Muslim University and is unconnected with Arya Samaj.

question: Swami Vivekananda attended the first Parliament of the World's Religions in 1893 at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chicago.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vivekananda represented Hinduism at the Parliament of the World's Religions held in Chicago in September 1893, raising the prestige of India and Hinduism abroad (शिकागो धर्म संसद 1893 में विवेकानंद)

 

• His address beginning with 'Sisters and Brothers of America' won wide acclaim and made him known across the West.

 

• He was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, and his original name was Narendra Nath Dutt.

 

• Back in India he turned his guru's message into organised social service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• He founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 and the Belur Math became its headquarters.

 

• Vivekananda lived from 1863 to 1902.

 

• The Mission's work covers relief, schools, hospitals and orphanages.

 

• Vivekananda returned to India in 1897 and spoke widely, and in 1899 he founded a second monastery at Belur. He also started two journals, the Prabuddha Bharata in English and the Udbodhan in Bengali.

 

NOTE

 

• London (Option 1): London was visited by Vivekananda later in 1895-96 for lectures, but the Parliament of Religions in 1893 was not held in the British capital.

 

• Paris (Option 3): Paris hosted the 1900 International Congress of the History of Religions, in which he participated, but this was seven years after the famous Parliament and is a separate event.

 

• New York (Option 4): New York was the city where the Theosophical Society was founded in 1875; Vivekananda founded a Vedanta Society there in 1894, but the 1893 Parliament occurred elsewhere in the American Midwest.

question: The Ramakrishna Mission was established in 1897 by Vivekananda at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belur Math, Howrah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vivekananda set up the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 with its headquarters at Belur Math, Howrah, in memory of his Guru Ramakrishna (रामकृष्ण मिशन — बेलूर मठ, हावड़ा)

 

• It is a social service and charitable society engaged in humanitarian relief and social work through schools, colleges, hospitals and orphanages.

 

• The Mission stresses service to humanity as service to God, a practical idea differing from purely ritual religion.

 

• Ramakrishna, a priest of the Kali temple, was known as the Dakshineswar Swami.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramakrishna taught the harmony of all religions and was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyay.

 

• Vivekananda's idea of Daridra Narayana made service to the poor into worship.

 

• Another Ramakrishna institution is the Advaita Ashrama at Mayavati.

 

• Besides Belur Math, the Mission runs the Advaita Ashrama at Mayavati and Vedanta centres abroad. Its monks work in disaster relief, and the Mission's motto stresses liberation of the self and welfare of the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Adyar, Madras (Option 2): Adyar, in Madras, became the headquarters of the Theosophical Society in 1882; it is therefore the centre of Blavatsky, Olcott and Besant's movement and not of the Ramakrishna Mission.

 

• Dakshineswar, Calcutta (Option 3): Dakshineswar near Calcutta was the temple where Ramakrishna worked as a priest, so it is associated with the Guru himself, whereas the Mission headquarters was placed at Belur on the Hooghly.

 

• Santiniketan, Birbhum (Option 4): Santiniketan in Birbhum was developed by Rabindranath Tagore as an educational ashram that later became Visva-Bharati, and is unrelated to the Mission founded by Vivekananda.

question: Which of the following is a correct statement about the Theosophical Society?
option_1: It was founded in 1882 at Adyar by Annie Besant
option_2: It was founded in 1875 in New York by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
option_3: It was founded in 1893 at Chicago by Vivekananda
option_4: It was founded in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang
solution_text:
The correct answer is It was founded in 1875 in New York by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Theosophical Society was established in 1875 in New York by Madame H.P. Blavatsky (Russia) and Colonel Henry Steel Olcott (USA) (थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी — न्यूयॉर्क, 1875)

 

• Its objectives were a universal brotherhood of man without distinction of race, colour or creed, and the study of ancient religions and philosophies.

 

• The headquarters moved to Adyar, Madras, in 1882.

 

• Annie Besant came to India in 1893 and took over the leadership after Olcott died in 1907.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besant also founded the Central Hindu School at Benaras in 1898, which led to the Banaras Hindu University (1916).

 

• She started the Home Rule League in 1916 and became Congress President in 1917.

 

• The Society glorified ancient Hindu doctrines such as karma and rebirth.

 

• Henry Steel Olcott, an American colonel, worked in Sri Lanka and India to revive Buddhism and Hindu education. Madame Blavatsky wrote 'Isis Unveiled' (1877) and 'The Secret Doctrine' (1888) as the Society's main works.

 

NOTE

 

• It was founded in 1882 at Adyar by Annie Besant (Option 1): Adyar became the headquarters in 1882, but the Society itself pre-dated this and was founded in New York; Annie Besant joined only in the early 1890s and led it after 1907.

 

• It was founded in 1893 at Chicago by Vivekananda (Option 3): Chicago in 1893 was the venue of the Parliament of Religions attended by Vivekananda, who started the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897; he was not the founder of the Theosophical Society.

 

• It was founded in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang (Option 4): The Prarthana Samaj was formed at Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang as a Brahmo-inspired movement; it is a different organisation founded in India rather than abroad.

question: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu School in 1898 at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banaras.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annie Besant set up the Central Hindu School in the city of Banaras during 1898; it later developed into the Banaras Hindu University (बनारस में सेंट्रल हिंदू स्कूल, 1898)

 

• She had arrived in India in 1893 and was associated with the Theosophical Society, whose headquarters stood at Adyar.

 

• After Colonel Olcott's death in 1907 she became president of the Society.

 

• Her educational work combined Hindu religious values with modern teaching.

 

• Besant's institution was therefore a school at Banaras for Hindu boys that mixed religious teaching with modern subjects, and it shows how Theosophists tried to support Hindu revival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madan Mohan Malaviya established the Banaras Hindu University in 1916, with the school as its nucleus.

 

• Besant launched the Home Rule League in September 1916.

 

• She became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917.

 

• Annie Besant's Central Hindu School was handed over to Madan Mohan Malaviya's Banaras Hindu University scheme. She also published the newspapers New India and Commonweal, which carried her Home Rule campaign.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore (Option 1): Lahore is the city of the first DAV School (1886) established by the Arya Samaj, whereas Besant's educational work centred on the holy city of Banaras.

 

• Poona (Option 2): Poona is linked to Jyotiba Phule's first girls' school of 1848 and the Satyashodak Samaj base; it was not the place where Besant started the Central Hindu School.

 

• Aligarh (Option 3): Aligarh was the site of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College of 1875, a Muslim educational institution that became a university, not Besant's Hindu school.

question: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Atmaram Pandurang.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 at Bombay by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, as an off-shoot of the Brahmo Samaj (प्रार्थना समाज की स्थापना — आत्माराम पांडुरंग, बंबई 1867)

 

• It was a reform movement within Hinduism, concentrating on inter-dining, inter-marriage, widow remarriage and the uplift of women and depressed classes.

 

• In 1870 Justice M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined and gave the Samaj new strength.

 

• The Samaj accepted the concepts of Karma and rebirth, and opposed child marriage and the caste system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ranade also helped found the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha and the Widow Marriage Association in Maharashtra.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen's visit to Bombay in 1864 had inspired the formation of the Samaj.

 

• Unlike the Brahmo Samaj it did not break entirely with Hindu traditions, staying close to the bhakti saints of Maharashtra.

 

• The Prarthana Samaj avoided the Brahmo break with idol-worshipping society and stressed devotional hymns of the Maharashtra saints. It founded night schools, orphanages and the Depressed Classes Mission in later years.

 

NOTE

 

• M.G. Ranade (Option 1): M.G. Ranade joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870 and became its most influential leader, but the founder in 1867 was Atmaram Pandurang, not Ranade.

 

• R.G. Bhandarkar (Option 3): R.G. Bhandarkar, the Sanskrit scholar, joined in 1870 alongside Ranade and strengthened the movement; he was not the person who established it three years earlier.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 4): Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj of India in Calcutta and visited Bombay, inspiring Prarthana Samaj leaders, but he did not found the Bombay body himself.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Prarthana Samaj:

1. It was an off-shoot of the Brahmo Samaj.

2. It rejected the doctrines of Karma and rebirth.

3. Justice M.G. Ranade joined it in 1870.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 3 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay) grew out of the Brahmo Samaj tradition and inspiration (कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: the Samaj accepted Karma and rebirth, a major difference from some Brahmo ideas, while opposing child marriage and caste.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined in 1870 and infused new strength.

 

• Its agenda covered inter-dining, intermarriage, widow remarriage and the uplift of women and depressed classes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ranade promoted the Social Conference as a platform for reformers, held alongside the Congress sessions.

 

• Bhandarkar was among the pioneers of Indological research in India.

 

• Prarthana Samaj leaders had links with Maharashtra's bhakti saints such as Tukaram.

 

• The Depressed Classes Mission was founded in 1906 by V.R. Shinde, a leader of the Prarthana Samaj. Ranade's Social Conference, organised from 1887 alongside Congress sessions, helped bring reform issues before national audiences.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 2): Combining statements 1 and 2 wrongly says the Samaj repudiated Karma and rebirth, whereas it retained these concepts, and it leaves out Ranade's 1870 entry that strengthened it.

 

• 2 only (Option 3): Statement 2 alone is incorrect on its own terms, since the Samaj accepted rebirth and karma; selecting it ignores the true statements about the Brahmo link and Ranade.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 4): Pairing statements 2 and 3 carries the false claim that Karma and rebirth were rejected, and omits statement 1 about the Samaj's Brahmo Samaj origin.

question: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodak Samaj in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1873.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phule launched the Satyashodak Samaj in 1873, aiming to fight the caste system and the dominance of Brahmins (सत्यशोधक समाज, 1873 — ज्योतिबा फुले)

 

• Phule belonged to a low-caste family of Maharashtra and waged a lifelong struggle against upper-caste domination and Brahmanical supremacy.

 

• He pioneered the widow remarriage movement in Maharashtra and worked for women's education.

 

• In the same year (1873) he wrote Gulamgiri, a critique of caste oppression.

 

• Since the Samaj accepted people of all castes, it challenged the monopoly of Brahmin priests in rituals, and its monthly ceremonies helped farmers and workers claim social dignity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Samaj sought to give lower castes access to religion without Brahmin priests.

 

• Phule's other works include Sarvajanik Satya Dharma Pustak.

 

• He is best known for social reforms and the anti-caste movement.

 

• Phule's Satyashodak Samaj admitted members of all castes and conducted marriages and ceremonies without Brahmin priests. His follower Narayan Meghaji Lokhande later organised Bombay's mill workers, and Phule was given the title Mahatma in 1888.

 

NOTE

 

• 1848 (Option 1): 1848 is the year Phule, with his wife Savitribai, opened the first girls' school at Poona, an earlier achievement and not the date of the Satyashodak Samaj.

 

• 1875 (Option 2): 1875 is associated with the Arya Samaj, the Theosophical Society and Sir Syed's Aligarh college, all different movements; Phule's Samaj was started two years earlier.

 

• 1890 (Option 4): 1890 is the year of Phule's death (he died in November 1890), so it cannot be the founding year of the organisation he started in the 1870s.

question: Savitribai Phule is remembered for:
option_1: Leading the Chandal movement in Bengal
option_2: Founding the first girls' school at Poona in 1848 with her husband
solution_text:
The correct answer is Founding the first girls' school at Poona in 1848 with her husband.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Savitribai Phule, with husband Jyotiba Phule, set up the first girls' school at Poona in 1848, and is regarded as India's first woman teacher (सावित्रीबाई फुले — पुणे में पहला बालिका विद्यालय, 1848)

 

• The couple faced fierce social opposition from orthodox groups for teaching girls and lower-caste children.

 

• Jyotiba is sometimes considered the first feminist of modern India for his championing of women's causes.

 

• The school's founding marked the real start of organised girls' education in western India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jyotiba also worked for the education of Dalits and widows.

 

• Phule's Gulamgiri (1873) compared caste slavery with American slavery.

 

• The Satyashodak Samaj was created in 1873.

 

• Savitribai Phule opened schools for girls from the Mahar and Mang castes and a care home for pregnant widows. She died in 1897, serving plague victims, and is honoured as the first woman teacher of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Leading the Chandal movement in Bengal (Option 1): The Chandal movement against untouchability in Bengal was led by Harichand Thakur, founder of the Matua sect; it is unrelated to Savitribai's educational mission in Poona.

 

• Founding the Theosophical Society (Option 3): The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 in New York by Blavatsky and Olcott, two foreigners, and has no link with the Phules or their schools.

 

• Starting the Self-Respect Movement (Option 4): The Self-Respect Movement began in 1925 in Tamil Nadu under E.V. Ramasamy Periyar; it came nearly eighty years after the Phules' school and belongs to another region.

question: The Widow Remarriage Act (1856) is associated with the efforts of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned for widow remarriage and protested against child marriage, and the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 legalised it (ईश्वरचंद्र विद्यासागर और विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम, 1856)

 

• He used Sanskrit scriptures to argue that the Shastras permitted remarriage of widows, answering orthodox critics on their own ground.

 

• He also supported women's education and helped in founding girls' schools in Bengal.

 

• The Act removed legal obstacles to the remarriage of Hindu widows, though social acceptance remained slow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidyasagar was the Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta.

 

• The Act was passed when Lord Canning was Governor-General, after drafts under Dalhousie.

 

• Phule and Ranade worked on the same cause in western India.

 

• Vidyasagar's Widow Remarriage Act is formally the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, XV of 1856. He also wrote Bornoporichoy, the Bengali primer, and as Inspector of Schools opened over thirty girls' schools in Bengal districts.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 1): Dayanand Saraswati also supported widow remarriage through the Arya Samaj, but the 1856 legal change was linked to the Bengal reformer's petitions, and Dayanand's work began after 1875.

 

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (Option 2): Sir Syed Ahmad Khan worked for educational advancement among Muslims at Aligarh and is not connected with the legislation on Hindu widows' remarriage.

 

• Annie Besant (Option 4): Annie Besant arrived in India only in 1893, nearly four decades after the Act, and her work concerned Theosophy and education, so she had no role in the 1856 law.

question: Saint Ramalinga founded the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam in 1865 to promote:
solution_text:
The correct answer is A casteless society.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saint Ramalinga (Vallalar) founded the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam in 1865 to promote a casteless society in Tamil Nadu (रामलिंग — जातिविहीन समाज हेतु संगम, 1865)

 

• His teaching stressed universal brotherhood, compassion for all beings and service to the poor over ritual and caste distinction.

 

• This places him among the regional social reformers of south India in the nineteenth century.

 

• The movement is one of several caste-challenging initiatives that preceded Periyar's Self-Respect Movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramalinga set up a free food kitchen at Vadalur that still functions.

 

• Veda Samaj of Madras (1864) also came from the same decade.

 

• Periyar E.V. Ramasamy later started the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.

 

• Ramalinga, also called Vallalar, preached jeevakarunya (compassion for life) and set up a free kitchen at Vadalur in 1867 that continues to feed visitors. He is regarded as a Tamil poet-saint whose verses form the Thiruarutpa.

 

NOTE

 

• Hindu-Muslim unity in politics (Option 1): Hindu-Muslim political unity was a theme of twentieth-century nationalism such as the Lucknow Pact of 1916; the Sangam of 1865 was a spiritual and social body.

 

• English education for women (Option 2): English education for women was promoted by figures like Vidyasagar and the Phules; Ramalinga's Sangam targeted caste barriers and religious uniformity through a universal spiritual path.

 

• Reconversion of Christians (Option 3): Reconversion of those who had embraced other faiths was the aim of the Suddhi movement of the Arya Samaj, not of Ramalinga's Tamil society.

question: E.V. Ramasamy Periyar started the Self-Respect Movement in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1925.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1925 E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar) began the Self-Respect Movement to uplift the Dravidians and expose Brahminical tyranny over all spheres of Hindu life (आत्म-सम्मान आंदोलन 1925 — पेरियार)

 

• The movement promoted equality, rationalism and anti-caste ideology among Tamil society.

 

• It questioned the authority of Brahmin priests and stressed dignity for non-Brahmins and women.

 

• Periyar worked first in the Congress before breaking away to lead this movement.

 

• The Self-Respect movement's positions on rationalism, women's equality and opposition to caste came to shape the political culture of Tamil Nadu in the following decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Periyar led the Vaikom Satyagraha in Kerala in 1924-25.

 

• His movement later became the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.

 

• The Justice Party had earlier voiced non-Brahmin claims in Madras Presidency.

 

• The Self-Respect Movement used journals like Kudi Arasu and promoted self-respect marriages without priests. Periyar was earlier Congress president of Tamil Nadu, resigned in 1925, and later renamed his group the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.

 

NOTE

 

• 1905 (Option 1): 1905 is the year Bengal was partitioned and the Swadeshi Movement began, not the year of the Tamil rationalist movement's launch twenty years later.

 

• 1937 (Option 2): 1937 saw the anti-Hindi agitation in Madras in which Periyar participated and the Congress ministries took office, but the Self-Respect Movement had started a dozen years before.

 

• 1947 (Option 4): 1947 is the year of Independence and Partition; Periyar was already an established social leader by then, and the Self-Respect movement long predated it.

question: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College at Aligarh in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1875.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (1817-98) founded the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875 to promote English education among Muslims (अलीगढ़ में MAO कॉलेज, 1875)

 

• The college later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University.

 

• His Aligarh Movement aimed at the social and educational advancement of Muslims by combining modern Western learning with Islam.

 

• He urged the community to accept scientific education and stay away from agitational politics.

 

• The college began as a school at Aligarh and gained college status in 1877, and the date 1875 refers to the original institution that evolved into the university.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Aligarh Movement is also linked with Syed Ahmad's journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq.

 

• He founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur (1864).

 

• AMU received university status in 1920.

 

• The foundation stone of the college was laid by Lord Lytton in 1877. The Mohammedan Educational Conference, founded by Sir Syed in 1886, spread his ideas on modern education across northern India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1857 (Option 1): 1857 was the year of the revolt, after which Sir Syed wrote about its causes, but it was not when the Aligarh college came into being.

 

• 1866 (Option 3): 1866 is the year Sir Syed formed the British Indian Association at Aligarh, a political-cum-social body, so it is not the founding year of the college.

 

• 1885 (Option 4): 1885 marks the founding of the Indian National Congress, which Sir Syed opposed and kept the Aligarh circle away from, ten years after his college was set up.

question: Where was the very first Singh Sabha formed in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritsar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The very first Singh Sabha was formed at Amritsar, the sacred city of Punjab, in 1873 (सिंह सभा आंदोलन — अमृतसर, 1873)

 

• The Sabha aimed at religious and social reform among the Sikhs and promoted modern education within the Sikh framework.

 

• Its leaders later set up the Khalsa College at Amritsar in 1892.

 

• Sikh reformers were responding to Christian missionary activity and Arya Samaj preaching in Punjab.

 

• Sikh intellectuals formed it to counter conversion and to revive Sikh traditions, and the Lahore Singh Sabha followed in 1879 with a more modern educated membership.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A second Singh Sabha was formed at Lahore in 1879 with a more radical profile.

 

• The Akali movement of the 1920s grew out of this reformist background.

 

• The Namdhari or Kuka movement under Guru Ram Singh arose earlier, in the mid-1800s.

 

• The Singh Sabha movement ran the Khalsa Diwan and the Khalsa Advocate paper, and its Sikh leaders included Thakur Singh Sandhawalia and Bhai Gurmukh Singh. Its work paved the way for the later Gurdwara reform of the 1920s.

 

NOTE

 

• Lahore (Option 1): Lahore got its own Singh Sabha in 1879, but the very first one was set up earlier in the Sikh holy city; Lahore is chiefly known for the DAV schools.

 

• Patiala (Option 2): Patiala was a princely state of Punjab and a patron of Sikh institutions, yet it did not host the first Singh Sabha of 1873.

 

• Ludhiana (Option 4): Ludhiana had missionary and military importance in Punjab, but it was not the city where Sikh reformers established the first Sabha.

question: The Khalsa College, Amritsar was established in 1892 by the leaders of the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Singh Sabha Movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khalsa College, Amritsar (1892) was set up by leaders of the Singh Sabha Movement to spread modern education among the Sikhs (अमृतसर में खालसा कॉलेज, 1892 — सिंह सभा)

 

• The movement began in Amritsar in 1873 and sought to reform Sikh religious and social practices.

 

• It tried to make Sikhs conscious of their separate identity while encouraging contemporary learning.

 

• The College became the main educational institution of the Sikh community in Punjab.

 

• The college was supported through donations from Sikh princely states and the community, and it trained generations of educated Sikhs for government service and the army.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chief Khalsa Diwan was founded in 1902 to coordinate Singh Sabhas.

 

• The Aligarh college of 1875 served Muslims, while the DAV college served the Arya Samaj.

 

• Sikh reform later led to the Gurdwara Reform movement and the SGPC (1920).

 

• The Chief Khalsa Diwan (1902) coordinated the many Singh Sabhas in Punjab. Khalsa College gave the community a modern institution, and Khalsa College Amritsar later also taught under Punjab University.

 

NOTE

 

• Aligarh Movement (Option 2): The Aligarh Movement built the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College for Muslims in 1875 and had no hand in a Sikh college in Amritsar.

 

• Suddhi Movement (Option 3): The Suddhi movement was the Arya Samaj's programme of reconversion to Hinduism; its educational wing created DAV institutions instead of Khalsa College.

 

• Satyashodak Movement (Option 4): The Satyashodak movement of Jyotiba Phule fought Brahmin dominance in Maharashtra, and it had no presence among Sikh reformers of Punjab.
